summary: R6-NEW-MAJ-001 (\S.{19,} non-whitespace anchor) is CLOSED — all-whitespace descriptions are now rejected. R6-NEW-MAJ-002 (§6 024B references regex literally) is CLOSED — the 024B acceptance row now explicitly says 'matching invariant 2's regex format spec literally'. R6-NEW-MAJ-003 (fail-closed default) is CLOSED — invariant 2 and §6 024B both enumerate the fourth CI behaviour (absent/unrecognised → exit non-zero). The mis-cased cascade-status bypass (e.g. 'Onboarded' capital O) is closed by the fail-closed default. However, one new MAJ finding surfaces: the R6 file-agnostic regex fix dropped the leading '- **' anchor but did NOT retain the trailing '**' after the slug. The plan-doc's own worked Example 1 — the canonical STATUS.md bold-marker format '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): description' — FAILS the current regex. grep -E returns exit code 1 on Example 1. This means check-invocation-log-entry.sh implementing the regex literally will reject legitimately-formatted TF rows in STATUS.md, breaking the onboarded-operator-bump CI check path. R7 fixpoint criterion (0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ on a complete cycle) is not met.

findings.title: Mis-cased cascade-status bypass ('Onboarded' capital O) — CLOSED by fail-closed default
findings.evidence: The enumerated set is {onboarded, onboarded-operator-bump, blocked-on-adopter-conflict} — all lowercase, hyphen-separated. The fail-closed default (invariant 2, plan-doc line 44) states: 'value not in the enumerated set → exit non-zero.' 'Onboarded' (capital O) is not in the enumerated set; the set comparison is case-sensitive by definition of exact-match enumeration. Similarly 'ONBOARDED', 'onboarded ' (trailing space), 'onboarded-operator_bump' (underscore), 'pending' — all fall outside the enumerated set and trigger the fail-closed exit. No mis-cased or near-miss value can bypass enforcement.
findings.outcome: CLOSED — the fail-closed default handles all case/whitespace/punctuation variants not in the exact enumeration

findings.title: Regex test — all 6 worked examples from plan-doc
findings.evidence: Current regex (plan-doc line 52): TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+ \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}. Test results: (1) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate disabled on PIM...' — Expected PASS, actual FAIL (grep -E returns exit code 1; Python re.search returns None). This is the plan-doc's canonical STATUS.md bold-format example. The regex engine matches the slug 'jrnb2024-pim' then requires ' (' as the next chars, but finds '**' (closing bold markers) instead — no match. (2) 'See TF-024X-conflict-jrnb2024-pim (pending): adopter has prior policy-check workflow...' — Expected PASS, actual PASS. (3) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim**' — Expected FAIL, actual FAIL. (4) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open):' — Expected FAIL, actual FAIL. (5) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open):                    ' — Expected FAIL, actual FAIL (\S anchor correctly blocks all-whitespace). (6) '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): short' — Expected FAIL, actual FAIL. Score: 5 of 6 behave as expected; Example 1 (STATUS.md bold format) fails when it should pass. See R7-NEW-MAJ-001.
findings.outcome: 1 of 6 worked examples behaves incorrectly — Example 1 (STATUS.md bold-marker format) fails the regex when it should pass

findings.title: Regex test — 3 reviewer-chosen additional edge cases
findings.evidence: Edge case 1 (Unicode NBSP U+00A0 at start of description): Input 'TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim (open): \u00A0this-is-a-description-definitely-long'. Python 3 re.search returns None — U+00A0 matches \s in Python 3 Unicode mode, so \S rejects it; CORRECT REJECTION. However, POSIX grep -E does not recognise U+00A0 as whitespace in many implementations; grep -E may ACCEPT this as a \S match. The spec says the regex is implemented in check-invocation-log-entry.sh but does not specify the regex engine. If implemented with grep -E (POSIX ERE), U+00A0 start descriptions could bypass the \S anchor. This is an implementation-ambiguity: the spec does not mandate the regex engine, so the U+00A0 behaviour is engine-dependent. MIN severity (requires a non-ASCII character in a description, which is unlikely in practice). Edge case 2 (nested parentheses in description): 'TF-024X-conflict-jrnb2024-ct (in-progress): Conflict with existing workflow (policy-check v2) needs rename PR' — Python re.search returns match; PASSES correctly. Nested parens in the description do not confuse the greedy .{19,} match. Edge case 3 (trailing whitespace after 20-char+ description): 'TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim (open): Renovate disabled on this adopter    ' — Python re.search returns match; PASSES correctly. Trailing whitespace does not prevent a valid match.
findings.outcome: Edge cases 2 and 3 behave correctly. Edge case 1 (U+00A0 NBSP) reveals an engine-dependent ambiguity; MIN severity.

findings.title: Regex does not match STATUS.md bold-marker format — plan-doc worked Example 1 fails the regex; check-invocation-log-entry.sh would reject legitimately-formatted TF rows for the onboarded-operator-bump path
findings.evidence: The fix-round-6 change made the regex file-agnostic by dropping the leading '^- \*\*' anchor from the R5 regex. However, the R5 regex also contained '\*\*' AFTER the slug (i.e. '...jrnb2024-pim\*\* \(open\)...') which was the closing bold marker for the STATUS.md format. The R6 file-agnostic regex retained the slug pattern '[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+' and then expects ' \(' (space then paren) immediately after the slug. In the STATUS.md bold format, the slug is followed by '**' (two asterisks — the closing bold marker) before the ' ('. The regex engine therefore finds: slug='jrnb2024-pim', next_expected=' (', actual_next='**' — NO MATCH. Verification: (a) Python 3 re.search(pattern, '- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): Renovate disabled on PIM; operator-bumped @abc123 at 024C; track until adopter enables Renovate cohort.') returns None. (b) grep -E 'TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+ \((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\): \S.{19,}' against Example 1 returns exit code 1 (no match). The DISPATCH-NOTE prose format (Example 2, no bold markers) still passes. The CONSEQUENCE is: check-invocation-log-entry.sh implementing the regex literally will exit non-zero when STATUS.md contains an onboarded-operator-bump TF row in the plan-doc's own canonical bold format. A Codex executor for 024B reading invariant 2 sees: (1) the regex, and (2) worked Example 1 showing the STATUS.md format as a passing case. The regex and the example contradict each other. One of the two is wrong; the regex is the normative spec, so Example 1 is 'wrong' by the regex — but Example 1 is also the intended STATUS.md format (confirmed by invariant 2 prose: 'appear in STATUS.md (the onboarded-operator-bump row in Tracked-forward items)'). This creates an ambiguity that will cause 024B implementers to either: (a) write the regex faithfully and produce a check that rejects correctly-formatted STATUS.md rows, or (b) deviate from the regex literal to handle the bold format. Neither is acceptable for a literal-regex implementation spec. SECURITY DIMENSION: The enforcement path for onboarded-operator-bump depends on the CI script finding the TF row in STATUS.md. If the script uses the regex literally and STATUS.md uses bold markers, the check exits non-zero — a false positive that causes CI to block a legitimate slice. The author, wanting CI to pass, may omit the '**' markers from the TF row, creating format drift between STATUS.md convention and the plan-doc's own Example 1. If the author, conversely, files the TF row with '**' markers (as Example 1 shows), CI blocks the slice, preventing onboarding. In either case, the enforcement chain for the onboarded-operator-bump meaningful-content gate is broken at the regex level. ROOT CAUSE: R6's file-agnostic fix correctly removed the leading '- **' anchor but inadvertently also removed the trailing '**' closing marker, making the regex unable to match the bold-wrapped form.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional non-capturing group for the trailing bold marker immediately after the slug pattern, before the space: change 'TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+ \((open|...)\): \S.{19,}' to 'TF-024X-(renovate|conflict)-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)+(?:\*\*)? \((open|...)\): \S.{19,}'. The '(?:\*\*)?' group is optional (zero or one occurrence) — it matches both the bold-wrapped STATUS.md format ('jrnb2024-pim** (open)') and the plain prose DISPATCH-NOTE format ('jrnb2024-pim (pending)'). Verify that worked Examples 1 and 2 both pass with the updated regex. Update the regex at invariant 2 line 52. The prose on line 55 does not need to change (it describes file-agnosticism, which this fix preserves). The §6 024B acceptance row references 'invariant 2's regex format spec literally' — once invariant 2 is fixed, 024B inherits the fix via the cross-reference, no separate §6 update needed.

findings.title: Residual near-stub bypass: \S.{19,} allows a single non-whitespace character followed by 19 whitespace chars (total 20 chars, only 1 meaningful)
findings.evidence: The regex \S.{19,} requires (a) the first character to be non-whitespace (\S) and (b) at least 19 more characters of any kind (.{19,}). A description of 'x' followed by 19 spaces (e.g. 'x                   ') has 20 chars total and passes: 'x' satisfies \S, 19 spaces satisfy .{19,}. Python re.search confirms: bool(re.search(pattern, 'TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim (open): x                   ')) == True. The plan-doc prose on line 55 says 'description starting with a non-whitespace character and ≥20 characters total' — this prose does technically permit 'x + 19 spaces' since it only requires the FIRST character to be non-whitespace, not all 20. R6-NEW-MAJ-001 was the all-whitespace bypass ('                    ' — 20 spaces fails \S anchor). The \S.{19,} fix closed that class but left open the minimal-content class: a single non-whitespace char followed by 19 spaces is not a meaningful description. This is a significantly narrower bypass than the R6 all-whitespace case (requires a deliberate attempt to write a near-empty description while front-loading a single non-whitespace char). Severity assessment: MIN. The spec's own prose is consistent with the regex in this regard; the prose explicitly condones 'starting with non-whitespace + ≥20 chars total'. A malicious actor would need to intentionally craft a near-empty description; a distracted actor would naturally write more than 1 meaningful character. No fix strictly required for R7 fixpoint, but a stronger regex (e.g. requiring ≥2 non-whitespace chars, or \S\S.{18,}) would fully close the near-stub class.
findings.recommendation: Optional hardening: change \S.{19,} to \S\S.{18,} (requires first two chars to be non-whitespace; total still ≥20) or \S\S\S.{17,} for belt-and-suspenders. The current \S.{19,} is consistent with the prose spec, so no change is strictly required for R7 fixpoint. If a future round hardens the meaningful-content threshold, this is the residual surface to address.
findings.outcome: NEW (MIN — residual near-stub bypass; no change strictly required for R7 fixpoint per prose spec alignment)

Conditional carve-out present; positive + negative assertions both stated. findings.title: Fail-closed default scope: does it cover ALL four branches (absent field, unrecognised value, 3 named values)?
findings.evidence: Invariant 2 (plan-doc line 44) text: 'if cascade-status: is absent OR contains a value not in the enumerated set {onboarded, onboarded-operator-bump, blocked-on-adopter-conflict}, the script exits non-zero (CI fails). Recognised values map to check-paths: (1) onboarded — [check-path]; (2) onboarded-operator-bump — [check-path]; (3) blocked-on-adopter-conflict — [check-path].' The fail-closed default uses 'OR' to combine two conditions: (a) field absent, (b) value not in enumerated set. This is comprehensive — any deviation from the three exact strings falls into condition (b). Case variants ('Onboarded'), whitespace variants ('onboarded '), underscore variants ('onboarded_operator_bump'), and entirely different values ('pending', 'approved') all fail condition (b). §6 024B acceptance row (plan-doc line 206) confirms: 'fail-closed default (absent or unrecognised value → exit non-zero)'. Both the spec and the acceptance contract are aligned. The DISPATCH-NOTE file itself being absent is addressed because the cascade-status: field is then absent, triggering condition (a).
findings.outcome: Fail-closed scope is complete. All four branches are covered.

r7_verdict_rationale: Three R6 closures are verified: R6-NEW-MAJ-001 (\S anchor), R6-NEW-MAJ-002 (§6 024B literal regex reference), R6-NEW-MAJ-003 (fail-closed default). The mis-cased cascade-status bypass is fully closed by the fail-closed default. One new MAJ finding surfaces: R7-NEW-MAJ-001. The R6 file-agnostic fix correctly removed the leading '- **' prefix anchor but inadvertently also dropped the trailing '**' closing bold marker from the slug segment. The result is that the regex cannot match the STATUS.md bold-formatted TF row format ('- **TF-024X-renovate-jrnb2024-pim** (open): description') which is the plan-doc's own canonical format shown in worked Example 1. The regex engine finds slug 'jrnb2024-pim', then expects ' (' as the next two chars, but finds '**' (closing bold markers) — no match. grep -E confirms exit code 1. check-invocation-log-entry.sh implementing the regex literally would therefore FAIL for correctly-formatted STATUS.md TF rows in the onboarded-operator-bump path, while the DISPATCH-NOTE prose format (no bold markers) continues to pass. This creates an enforcement gap: the bold-format STATUS.md row that the plan-doc mandates cannot be verified by the spec's own regex. One new MIN finding: R7-RESIDUAL-MIN-001 (\S.{19,} allows single-char meaningful content followed by 19 trailing spaces — a near-stub bypass narrower than R6's all-whitespace class but still present).
